summary: Built M2-S01 (access, scale project, build_mode design-only): the Bypass_Opportunity_Sales_Validation custom permission and the Sales_Ops_Validation_Bypass permission set that grants it, plus the step's package.xml and deploy-order.md. Four declared outputs written, nothing else. The custom permission carries only <description> and <label> (no <isLicensed>, no <requiredPermission>, no <connectedApp>); the permission set carries <label>, <description>, <hasActivationRequired>false and exactly one <customPermissions> node - no objectPermissions, no fieldPermissions, no userPermissions, no license - which is what the step's manual acceptance test requires a human to be able to read off the file. Element names and enum values come only from skills/admin/custom-permissions/references/metadata-examples.md (sections 2 and 5, 'Where the files live', 'package.xml') and skills/admin/permission-set-architecture/references/metadata-examples.md (sections 1, 2, 5); the shapes match the org-validated precedent at examples/builds/case-onboarding/artefacts/M2-S01/. Both declared checkers exited 0 on the first pass with zero repair passes; all three *.xml files parse; check-outputs returned ok. Two prose divergences from the plan's own test descriptions are recorded rather than papered over: the custom-permissions checker printed 0 info (not the 1 info the planner's fixture saw) because the description was trimmed to 197 characters as inputs.note asked, and at build scope it printed Consumers 0 (not 1) because M2-S03's validation rule does not exist yet.
confidence_rationale: Step 10 MEDIUM on one count: documented skill defaults stood in for two Questions-to-Ask rows no clarification answers - hasActivationRequired=false (the value both cited references write out on purpose) for 'Does any permission need step-up activation?', and an omitted <license> for 'Which user or permission set license does every person in this persona hold?' (Q19 names profiles, not licences). Everything else in the HIGH row holds: every element traced to the Step 3 inventory, both cited checkers exited 0 on the first pass, check-outputs ok, every declared output written and nothing else.

dimensions_skipped.reason: Three Questions-to-Ask rows across the two access skills could not be answered from the plan. (1) custom-permissions 'Does anything already hold this access through a profile?' - unanswerable in a design-only build: it needs the SetupEntityAccess baseline query against a live org, which this agent may not run. (2) custom-permissions / permission-set-architecture 'Should any of this expire?' - no answered clarification puts an end date on the grant; it was treated as a standing capability of the sales-ops admin role and no expiring assignment was designed. (3) permission-set-architecture 'Which user or permission set license does every person in this persona hold?' - Q19 answers in profiles (System Administrator for the sales-ops admin), not in licences, so <license> was left out per the Object Reference guidance quoted in the skill.

process_observations.observation: Both declared checkers exited 0 on the first pass with zero repair passes, and the permission-set checker printed the exact string the planner recorded from its fixture run ('No issues found.').

The plan sized this step to exactly what the two skills can ground: every element the step needed (description, label, hasActivationRequired, customPermissions/enabled+name, and the two package.xml types) is in a fenced example in a cited skill, so the Step 3 gap rule never came close to firing.

The step's first acceptance-test description narrates fixture output this run did not reproduce: it says step scope printed 'Summary: 0 error(s), 0 warning(s), 1 info.' and build scope printed 'Consumers 1', while this run printed 0 info at both scopes (the description was trimmed to 197 characters, under the CP-DESC-02 threshold, exactly as the step's own inputs.note asked) and Consumers 0 at both scopes (M2-S03's validation rule is not built yet, so nothing in artefacts/ names the permission).

evidence.detail: steps[M2-S01].acceptance_tests[0].description vs the run recorded in extensions.checker_results

process_observations.observation: inputs.note asks for a description under 200 characters while acceptance_tests[0].description records a fixture that raised CP-DESC-02 (which only fires at 200+), so the two cannot both describe the shipped file; the note was followed because step inputs are the higher-priority source and CP-DESC-02 is headroom the build does not have to spend.

This step's artefacts validate green on their own whether or not the bypass is ever wired to anything: a validation rule whose $Permission token names a permission the org lacks evaluates to false silently rather than failing the deploy (custom-permissions gotcha 4), so a green M2-S01 deploy is not evidence the discount cap has an escape hatch - only a run that carries M2-S03 with it is.

Nothing in this build assigns the permission set, and nothing in it can: PermissionSetAssignment is record data inserted through Apex or Data Loader, so the sentence 'the sales-ops admin is the only person who can save past that rule' in the M2 milestone goal is true of the design and unproven of any org until someone runs the SetupEntityAccess query in deploy-order.md section 4.

decision_record.question: custom-permissions: 'What exactly does holding this permission let someone do, in one sentence?'
decision_record.answer: It suppresses the Opportunity sales validation rules for its holder - one sentence, no 'and', so one permission rather than two.

decision_record.question: custom-permissions: 'Is this a bypass? If so, which named rules does it suppress?'
decision_record.answer: Yes. Opportunity_Discount_Requires_Approval (M2-S03) and Opportunity_Products_Required_At_Propose (M2-S04), both of which put NOT($Permission.Bypass_Opportunity_Sales_Validation) first inside their outer AND.
